name: ioctl
synopsis: int ioctl(int fd, unsigned long op, ...); /* glibc, BSD */
int ioctl(int fd, int op, ...); /* musl, other UNIX */
description: The ioctl() system call manipulates the underlying device parameters of special files, particularly character special files like terminals. It requires an open file descriptor, a device-dependent operation code, and an argument pointer.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the open file

parameters.name: op
parameters.description: Device-dependent operation code (or int in some variants)

parameters.name: argp
parameters.description: Pointer to memory for the argument

return_value.success: Usually returns zero; some operations return a nonnegative value.
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set.

errors.description: fd is not a valid file descriptor.
argp references an inaccessible memory area.
op or argp is not valid.
fd is not associated with a character special device or the operation does not apply.

bugs: The size bits in ioctl op values are unreliable due to buggy macros or legacy values, and the structure can vary across architectures.
versions: Varies by system; historically from Version 7 AT&T UNIX, with variations in SysIII, 4.3BSD, and SysVr4.
